chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin from his brother al-Husayn from Ali ibn Yaqtin who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the sale of the mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon the master's death). He said: If the master gave permission for it, there is no harm in it. And if there was a debt upon the master of the slave, and he manumitted him to escape the debt, his manumission is not valid. And if he manumitted him while healthy, the creditor has no claim against him, and his manumission proceeds.

key_terms.الْمُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave manumitted upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling a mudabbir slave if the master has outstanding debts?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfahani's al-Istibsar clarifies the conditions under which a mudabbir (a slave emancipated upon the master's death) may be sold, distinguishing between voluntary sale and sale to evade debt. It establishes that if the master is healthy when authorizing the sale, the transaction is final and creditors cannot reclaim the slave, whereas a sale motivated by debt evasion renders the manumission void. This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the master's intent and financial status in determining the validity of the slave's path to freedom.
